Mandloi, learned counsel appearing for the complainant / objector has also opposed the prayer and it is submitted that the applicant has duped the complainant party to the tune of Rs.1,00,00,000/- (rupees one crore) by selling them a property which was already sold and was not owned by the applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Anil vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: Thus, it is submitted that no case for grant of bail is made out.
sentences._hearing_file: Anil vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Having considered the rival submissions and on perusal of the case diary, it is found that although the applicant has stated that some agreements were fraudulently executed through him, but there is nothing on record to suggest that the lands regarding which the agreements were entered into by the applicant and the complainant side, was not sold by the applicant prior to entering into agreement with the complainant party; and in such circumstances, this Court does not find it to be a fit case to extend the benefit of bail in favour of the applicant, who appears to be involved in a large scale of fraud.
Thus, the application being devoid of merits is hereby dismissed.
Pending interlocutory application, if any, shall stands disposed of.
